answer: The tide cap is enforced at intake and trellis shows the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool as a result cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch however much capital it holds, because every participant consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. At most 2 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a mirror tag. That is 2 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
